title: The agent logs nothing across a stall: no subscriber in the test harness
description:
The agent daemon logged nothing across a multi-minute stall, and the
test harness that started it installs no `tracing` subscriber, so even
the daemon's own events went nowhere. Characterising bead mimid-604m
took three runs of the same test because of this: the only timeline
available came from the test's own wait helpers, which can say what
they are waiting for but not what the daemon is doing.

## Two halves

1. **The harness.** `crates/mimid-agent/tests/common/mod.rs` builds the
   daemon in-process and never calls `tracing_subscriber`. Install one
   per test process, writing to the captured test output, honouring
   `RUST_LOG`, defaulting to a level that is quiet on a passing run.
   `tracing_subscriber::fmt().with_test_writer()` with
   `EnvFilter::from_default_env()` is the shape; the subscriber is
   global, so it goes behind a `OnceLock`/`LazyLock` and tolerates a
   second call.

2. **The daemon.** Find what the first-DM path does between the user's
   action and the reply, and make sure each step that can block says so
   at a level a stalled user's log would show: the sync, the KeyPackage
   fetch, the Welcome, each SQLite transaction. A step that takes
   seconds and logs nothing is the defect; the fix is a span around it,
   not a println.

## Constraint

AGENTS.md: secrets never reach logs, secret-bearing types redact
`Debug`, and the canary test that captures `tracing` output and proves
no secret appears in it must still pass with the new events in place.
Run it after adding any field.

## Why it is worth doing first

The other two children of mimid-604m are searches for where time goes.
Both are much cheaper once the daemon says what it is doing.
